issue.title: Adopt SSH publickey credential retries in sidecar push, AXE sidecar runner, finalizer pushes, and bead sync

task_type_fields.proposal:
Extend the SSH publickey credential-retry policy that epic sase-1r5.1 added
(`src/sase/git_credential_retry.py`: `CredentialRetry`, `LAUNCH_CREDENTIAL_RETRY_BUDGET`,
`BACKGROUND_CREDENTIAL_RETRY_BUDGET`, kill switch `SASE_GIT_CREDENTIAL_RETRY_MAX_SECONDS`)
to the git network call sites that never consult sase-core's retryability classifier.
During an incident like GitHub's 2026-11-04 one, these sites still fail on the first
transient `Permission denied (publickey)`. Phase sase-1r5.1.5 proposed all four
(notes #1-#4 on that bead):

1. `src/sase/sdd/_sidecar_git.py` `push_sidecar`: runs `run_sdd_git(..., check=True)`
   with no retry or classifier, so the sidecar-init push fails at once with
   `SddMaterializationError`. User-visible.
2. `src/sase/axe/runner_workspace_sidecar.py`: the `default_git_runner` fetch/merge/push
   calls (`_run_sidecar_push`, `decide_sidecar_publication_after_push`) retry only
   divergence, never auth. Sidecar publication and safety checks fail at once.
   User-visible in AXE runs.
3. Host finalizer pushes in `src/sase/vcs_provider/plugins/_git_commit_dispatch.py`
   (`_push_with_retry`, `_push_current_branch_with_rebase_retry`): they retry only
   branch collisions and remote movement, so a denial aborts the stitch landing push.
   User-visible.
4. The bead sync worker (`src/sase/bead/_sync_worker_run.py`): it retries only push races
   (`is_retryable_push_race`). A denial fails that sync pass, but the next tick recovers
   it, so this is a delayed sync rather than an abort. Lowest priority; the worker may
   decline it with a recorded reason.

For each site, classify the failure with `classify_failure_retryability` (the git
operation kind). On `RETRYABILITY_VERDICT_CREDENTIAL_UNCONFIRMED`, consult one
`CredentialRetry` per logical operation and keep git's original stderr first, appending
`failure_suffix()`. Choose the budget per site. Turn-end finalizer pushes and AXE
background work probably want the background budget, and only launch-blocking work
should take the 110s launch budget. Never sleep while holding a lock or admission permit.
Follow the adopted examples in `sdd/_store_clone_remote.py`, `sdd/_git_network.py`, and
`workspace_provider/_lease_git.py`, including their tests (ssh shim in
`tests/sdd_store/test_sidecar_clone_retry_credentials.py`). Reset
`sase.git_credential_retry._EXHAUSTED_HOSTS` in tests. Update the budget list in
`docs/reference/agents/service-host.md` and `docs/contribute/sdd-storage.md`.
task_type_fields.why_out_of_scope:
Epic sase-1r5.1's plan scoped adoption to call sites that already consult the
classifier (SDD store clone, SDD network git, operational-lease fetch). Its inventory
marked these non-classifier sites out of scope and had phase docs-and-followups record
them as proposed follow-ups.

issue.creation_reason: Epic sase-1r5.1 made SSH publickey denials retryable only where the classifier was already consulted; its phase sase-1r5.1.5 found four more network git sites that still abort on the first transient denial, and the epic's land agent is filing them as one follow-up.
